title_en: Law of the People's Republic of China on the Promotion of Private Economy

articles.content_en: Article 1 This Law is enacted in accordance with the Constitution to optimize the environment for the development of the private economy, ensure that all types of economic organizations participate in market competition on an equal footing, promote the healthy development of the private economy and the healthy growth of private entrepreneurs, build a high-level socialist market economy system, and give play to the important role of the private economy in national economic and social development.

Article 2 The work of promoting the development of the private economy shall adhere to the leadership of the Communist Party of China, adhere to a people-centered development philosophy, and adhere to the socialist system with Chinese characteristics, so as to ensure the correct political direction for the development of the private economy.
The State upholds and improves the basic socialist economic systems, including the system with public ownership as the mainstay and diverse forms of ownership developing together, the system with distribution according to work as the mainstay and multiple forms of distribution coexisting, and the socialist market economy system; unswervingly consolidates and develops the public sector of the economy, and unswervingly encourages, supports, and guides the development of the non-public sector of the economy; fully leverages the decisive role of the market in resource allocation, and better plays the role of the government.

Article 3 The private economy is an important component of the socialist market economy, a vital force in advancing Chinese-style modernization, an important foundation for high-quality development, and an important force in promoting the comprehensive building of a modern socialist country and realizing the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Promoting sustained, healthy, and high-quality development of the private economy is a major long-term policy and guideline of the State.
The State shall encourage, support, and guide the development of the private economy in accordance with law, and better play the role of the rule of law in consolidating foundations, stabilizing expectations, and ensuring long-term benefits.
The State adheres to the principles of equal treatment, fair competition, equal protection, and common development to promote the growth and expansion of the private economy. Private economic organizations and other types of economic organizations shall enjoy equal legal status, market opportunities, and development rights.

Article 4 The State Council and local people's governments at or above the county level shall incorporate the work of promoting the development of the private economy into national economic and social development plans, establish coordination mechanisms for promoting the development of the private economy, formulate and improve policies and measures, and coordinate to solve major problems in the development of the private economy.
The development and reform department of the State Council shall be responsible for the overall coordination of the work of promoting the development of the private economy. Other relevant departments of the State Council shall, within their respective duties, be responsible for the relevant work of promoting the development of the private economy.
Relevant departments of local people's governments at or above the county level shall carry out the work of promoting the development of the private economy in accordance with laws and regulations and the division of duties determined by the people's government at the same level.

Article 5 Private economic organizations and their operators shall support the leadership of the Communist Party of China, adhere to the socialist system with Chinese characteristics, and actively devote themselves to the construction of a modern socialist country.
The State shall strengthen the construction of the contingent of operators of private economic organizations, strengthen ideological and political guidance, and give play to their important role in economic and social development; cultivate and promote the spirit of entrepreneurship, guide operators of private economic organizations to practice socialist core values, be patriotic and dedicated, operate in compliance with law, engage in entrepreneurship and innovation, give back to society, and firmly commit to being builders of socialism with Chinese characteristics and promoters of Chinese-style modernization.

Article 6 Private economic organizations and their operators, when engaging in production and business activities, shall abide by laws and regulations, observe social morality and commercial ethics, act in good faith and compete fairly, fulfill social responsibilities, protect the legitimate rights and interests of workers, safeguard national interests and social public interests, and accept supervision from the government and society.

Article 7 The Federation of Industry and Commerce shall play an important role in promoting the healthy development of the private economy and the healthy growth of private entrepreneurs, strengthen the ideological and political construction of operators of private economic organizations, guide private economic organizations to operate in accordance with law, and improve the level of services for the private economy.

Article 8 Strengthen the publicity and reporting of advanced deeds such as innovation and creation of private economic organizations and their operators, support private economic organizations and their operators to participate in appraisals and commendations, guide the formation of a social environment that respects labor, respects creation, and respects entrepreneurs, and create an atmosphere where the whole society cares about, supports, and promotes the development of the private economy.

Article 9 The State shall establish and improve a statistical system for the private economy, conduct statistical analysis on the development of the private economy, and regularly release relevant information.

Article 10 The State shall implement a nationwide unified negative list system for market access. In fields other than those on the negative list for market access, various types of economic organizations, including private economic organizations, may enter equally in accordance with law.

Article 11 People's governments at all levels and their relevant departments shall implement the fair competition review system. Policies and measures involving the production and business activities of business entities shall be subject to fair competition review, and shall be periodically assessed, and policies and measures containing content that hinders a unified national market and fair competition shall be promptly amended or abolished to ensure that private economic organizations participate in market competition on an equal footing.
The market supervision and administration department shall be responsible for accepting reports on policies and measures that violate the fair competition review system and handling them according to law.

Article 12 The State shall ensure that private economic organizations, in accordance with law, equally use capital, technology, human resources, data, land and other natural resources, and other factors of production and public service resources, and equally apply the State's supporting development policies.

Article 13 People's governments at all levels and their relevant departments, in accordance with their statutory authority, shall treat private economic organizations equally when formulating and implementing policies and measures concerning government fund arrangements, land supply, pollutant discharge indicators, public data opening, qualification permits, standard setting, project declaration, professional title evaluation, evaluation and award selection, human resources, and other aspects.

Article 14 Public resource trading activities shall be open, transparent, fair, and just, and shall treat all types of economic organizations, including private economic organizations, equally in accordance with law.
Unless otherwise provided by law, public resource transactions such as bids and tenders, and government procurement shall not have acts that restrict or exclude private economic organizations.

Article 15 Anti-monopoly and anti-unfair competition law enforcement agencies, in accordance with their duties and authority, shall prevent and suppress monopolistic and unfair competition conduct in market economic activities, handle conduct that abuses administrative power to exclude or restrict competition according to law, and provide a good market environment for private economic organizations.

Article 16 Support private economic organizations to participate in major national strategies and major projects. Support private economic organizations to invest and start businesses in strategic emerging industries, future industries, and other fields, encourage them to carry out technological transformation and transformation and upgrading of traditional industries, and participate in the investment and construction of modern infrastructure.

Article 17 Relevant departments of the State Council shall, based on the national major development strategies, development plans, industrial policies, etc., coordinate research and formulate policies and measures to promote investment by the private economy, publish information on major projects that encourage investment by the private economy, and guide the private economy to invest in key areas.
Private economic organizations that invest and construct fixed asset investment projects that conform to the national strategic direction shall enjoy the State's supporting policies according to law.

Article 18 Support private economic organizations to revitalize existing assets through various means, improve their reinvestment capacity, and enhance asset quality and efficiency.
People's governments at all levels and their relevant departments shall support private economic organizations to participate in government and social capital cooperation projects. Government and social capital cooperation projects shall reasonably set the rights and obligations of both parties, and specify matters such as the method of obtaining investment returns, risk-sharing mechanism, and dispute resolution methods.

Article 19 People's governments at all levels and their relevant departments shall provide standardized, efficient, and convenient services for private economic organizations in terms of project promotion and matchmaking, preliminary work and processing of approval matters, factor acquisition, and government investment support.

Article 20 Relevant departments of the State Council shall, based on their functions, play the incentive and constraining role of monetary policy tools and macro-credit policies, implement differentiated policies for financial institutions providing financial services to small and micro private economic organizations in accordance with market-oriented and rule-of-law principles, supervise and guide financial institutions to reasonably set tolerance for non-performing loans, establish and improve due diligence exemption mechanisms, enhance professional service capabilities, and improve the level of financial services provided to private economic organizations.

Article 21 Banking financial institutions and others shall, in accordance with laws and regulations, accept guarantee methods that meet the needs of loan business, and provide private economic organizations with pledge loans of rights such as accounts receivable, warehouse receipts, equity, and intellectual property rights.
People's governments at all levels and their relevant departments shall provide support and convenience for the registration, valuation, transaction circulation, and information sharing of movable property and rights pledges.

Article 22 The State shall promote the establishment and improvement of market-oriented risk-sharing mechanisms for private economic organizations' financing, support banking financial institutions and financing guarantee institutions to expand business cooperation in an orderly manner, and jointly serve private economic organizations.

Article 23 Financial institutions shall, on the premise of compliance with laws and regulations and in accordance with market-oriented and sustainable development principles, develop and provide financial products and services suitable for the characteristics of the private economy, provide convenient conditions for creditworthy private economic organizations to obtain financing, enhance the adaptability of credit supply and loan cycles to the financing needs and capital use cycles of private economic organizations, and improve the availability and convenience of financial services.

Article 24 Financial institutions shall treat private economic organizations equally in terms of credit granting, credit management, risk control management, service charges, etc.
If financial institutions, in violation of the agreement with the private economic organization borrower, unilaterally increase the conditions for granting loans, suspend the granting of loans, or recover loans before maturity, they shall bear liability for breach of contract according to law.
Article 25 Improve the multi-level capital market system, support qualified private economic organizations to obtain direct financing on an equal footing through issuing stocks, bonds, etc.

Article 26 Establish and improve the credit information collection and sharing mechanism, support credit investigation agencies to provide credit investigation services for private economic organizations' financing, support credit rating agencies to optimize the rating methods of private economic organizations, increase the effective supply of credit ratings, and provide convenience for private economic organizations to obtain financing.

Article 27 The State shall encourage and support private economic organizations to actively play a role in promoting scientific and technological innovation, cultivating new quality productive forces, and building a modern industrial system. Guide private economic organizations to strengthen basic and frontier research, develop key core technologies, common basic technologies, and frontier cross-cutting technologies based on national strategic needs, industry development trends, and global scientific and technological frontiers, promote the integrated development of scientific and technological innovation and industrial innovation, and foster new industries, new models, and new driving forces.
Guide non-profit funds to fund private economic organizations to conduct basic research, frontier technology research, and social welfare technology research according to law.

Article 28 Support private economic organizations to participate in national science and technology research projects, support capable private economic organizations to take the lead in undertaking national major technology research tasks, open national major scientific research infrastructure to private economic organizations, support public research and development platforms and common technology platforms to open and share, provide equal services for private economic organizations' technological innovation, encourage various enterprises and higher education institutions, research institutes, and vocational schools to innovate cooperation mechanisms with private economic organizations, carry out technical exchanges and achievement transformation, and promote deep integration of industry, academia, and research.

Article 29 Support private economic organizations to participate in digital, intelligent common technology research and development and data factor market construction according to law, reasonably use data according to law, develop and utilize open public data resources, enhance data factor sharing, inclusiveness, and security, and give full play to the enabling role of data.

Article 30 The State shall ensure that private economic organizations participate in the formulation of standards according to law, and strengthen information disclosure and public supervision of standard formulation.
The State shall provide private economic organizations with services and conveniences in scientific research infrastructure, technical verification, standards and specifications, quality certification, inspection and testing, intellectual property, demonstration application, and other aspects.

Article 31 Support private economic organizations to strengthen the application of new technologies, carry out application experiments of new technologies, new products, new services, and new models, give play to the role of technology markets and intermediary service institutions, and promote the application and promotion of scientific and technological achievements through various means.
Encourage private economic organizations to voluntarily conduct technical cooperation based on commercial rules during the investment process. The conditions for technical cooperation shall be negotiated and determined by the parties to the investment based on the principle of fairness.

Article 32 Encourage private economic organizations to actively cultivate and employ knowledge-based, skill-based, and innovative talents, cultivate and employ highly skilled talents in key positions and key processes, and promote the construction of the industrial worker team.

Article 33 The State shall strengthen the protection of original innovation by private economic organizations and their operators. Increase the protection of intellectual property rights of innovation achievements, implement a punitive compensation system for intellectual property infringement, and investigate and handle illegal acts such as infringement of trademark exclusive rights, patent rights, copyrights, and trade secrets, counterfeiting and confusion according to law.
Strengthen regional and departmental coordination of intellectual property protection, and provide private economic organizations with services such as rapid collaborative protection of intellectual property, diversified dispute resolution, rights protection assistance, and guidance for overseas intellectual property dispute response and risk warning.

Article 34 The organizations and members of the Communist Party of China in private economic organizations shall carry out Party activities in accordance with the Constitution of the Communist Party of China and relevant intra-party regulations, and play the political leading role of Party organizations and the vanguard and exemplary role of Party members in promoting the healthy development of private economic organizations.

Article 35 Private economic organizations shall focus on the overall work of the country, actively play a role in economic development, expanding employment, improving people's livelihood, scientific and technological innovation, etc., and contribute to meeting the people's growing needs for a better life.

Article 36 Private economic organizations engaging in production and business activities shall abide by laws and regulations on labor employment, work safety, occupational health, social security, ecological environment, quality standards, intellectual property, network and data security, fiscal taxation, finance, etc.; shall not obtain improper benefits through bribery, fraud, and other means, and shall not disrupt market and financial order, damage the ecological environment, harm the legitimate rights and interests of workers, and social public interests.
State organs shall supervise and manage the production and business activities of private economic organizations according to law.

Article 37 Support private capital to serve economic and social development, improve the rules and systems of capital behavior, regulate and guide the healthy development of private capital according to law, and maintain the order of the socialist market economy and social public interests. Support private economic organizations to strengthen risk prevention and management, encourage private economic organizations to optimize their main businesses and strengthen their real industries, and enhance core competitiveness.

Article 38 Private economic organizations shall improve corporate governance structure and management systems, regulate operator behavior, strengthen internal supervision, and achieve standardized governance; establish and improve the democratic management system with the workers' congress as the basic form according to law. Encourage qualified private economic organizations to establish and improve modern enterprise systems with Chinese characteristics.
Trade unions and other mass organizations in private economic organizations shall carry out activities in accordance with laws and charters, strengthen the ideological and political guidance of workers, protect the legitimate rights and interests of workers, play a role in the democratic management of enterprises, promote the improvement of the collective wage negotiation system for enterprises, and promote the construction of harmonious labor relations.
The organizational form, organizational structure, and operating rules of private economic organizations shall be governed by the provisions of laws such as the Company Law of the People's Republic of China, the Partnership Enterprise Law of the People's Republic of China, and the Sole Proprietorship Enterprise Law of the People's Republic of China.

Article 39 The State shall promote the establishment of a mechanism for private economic organizations to prevent and combat corruption at the source, support and guide private economic organizations to establish and improve internal audit systems, strengthen integrity risk prevention and control, promote private economic organizations to improve their compliance management level according to law, and promptly prevent, discover, and manage illegal and non-compliant issues in operations.
Private economic organizations shall strengthen legal education for their staff, and create a culture of integrity, honesty, compliance, and law-abiding.

Article 40 Private economic organizations shall, in accordance with laws, administrative regulations, and the unified accounting system of the State, strengthen financial management, standardize accounting, prevent financial fraud, and distinguish the production and business income and expenditure of private economic organizations from the personal income and expenditure of operators of private economic organizations, and achieve the separation of the property of private economic organizations from the personal property of operators of private economic organizations.

Article 41 Support private economic organizations to promote employees sharing development results by strengthening skills training, expanding employment absorption, improving wage distribution systems, etc.

Article 42 Explore the establishment of a social responsibility evaluation system and incentive mechanism for private economic organizations, encourage and guide private economic organizations to actively fulfill social responsibilities, and voluntarily participate in public welfare and charitable activities, emergency disaster relief, etc.

Article 43 Private economic organizations and their operators, when investing and operating overseas, shall abide by the laws of the country or region where they are located, respect local customs and cultural traditions, maintain the national image, and shall not engage in activities that harm national security and national interests.

Article 44 State organs and their staff shall perform their duties according to law in the work of promoting the development of the private economy. State functionaries and operators of private economic organizations, in their work interactions, shall abide by laws and discipline, and maintain integrity and honesty.
People's governments at all levels and their relevant departments shall establish a smooth and effective government-enterprise communication mechanism, promptly listen to the opinions and suggestions of various economic organizations including private economic organizations, and solve reasonable problems reflected by them.

Article 45 When State organs formulate laws, regulations, rules, and other normative documents closely related to the production and business activities of business entities, when the Supreme People's Court and the Supreme People's Procuratorate make interpretations of specific legal applications in trial and procuratorial work, or make major decisions, they shall pay attention to listening to the opinions and suggestions of various economic organizations including private economic organizations, industry associations, and chambers of commerce; before implementation, they shall leave a necessary adaptation and adjustment period based on actual conditions.
In accordance with the provisions of the Legislation Law of the People's Republic of China, laws, regulations, rules, and other normative documents closely related to the production and business activities of business entities, and interpretations of specific legal applications in trial and procuratorial work, shall not have retroactive effect, except for special provisions made to better protect the rights and interests of citizens, legal persons, and other organizations.

Article 46 People's governments at all levels and their relevant departments shall promptly disclose to the public the scope, standards, conditions, and application procedures for preferential policies involving business entities, and provide convenience for private economic organizations to apply for and enjoy relevant preferential policies.

Article 47 People's governments at all levels and their relevant departments shall formulate policies to encourage private economic organizations to start businesses, provide public services, and encourage entrepreneurship to drive employment.

Article 48 Registration authorities shall provide all types of economic organizations, including private economic organizations, with legally compliant, standardized and unified, open and transparent, convenient and efficient registration services for establishment, change, and deregistration, and reduce market entry and exit costs.
Individual industrial and commercial households may voluntarily transform into enterprises according to law. Registration authorities, tax authorities, and relevant departments shall provide guidance and convenience for individual industrial and commercial households to transform into enterprises.

Article 49 Encourage and support higher education institutions, research institutes, vocational schools, public training bases, and various vocational skill training institutions to innovate talent training models, strengthen vocational education and training, and cultivate professional talents and industrial workers that meet the high-quality development needs of the private economy.
Human resources and social security departments shall establish and improve human resources service mechanisms, build information matching platforms for recruitment and job seeking, and provide convenience for private economic organizations to recruit and employ workers.
People's governments at all levels and their relevant departments shall improve talent incentive and service guarantee policies and measures, smooth the channels for professional title evaluation of private economic organizations, and provide support for private economic organizations to introduce and cultivate high-level and urgently needed talents.

Article 50 Administrative organs shall adhere to administration according to law. Administrative organs, when conducting law enforcement activities, shall avoid or minimize impacts on the normal production and business activities of private economic organizations, and promptly respond to and handle their reasonable and lawful demands.

Article 51 Administrative penalties for violations of law by private economic organizations and their operators shall be implemented in accordance with the same principles as those applied to other economic organizations and their operators. Where an administrative penalty or other measure is required by law for a violation, it shall be commensurate with the facts, nature, circumstances, and degree of social harm of the violation. Where a violation falls under the circumstances for lighter, mitigated, or exemption from punishment as provided for in the Administrative Penalty Law of the People's Republic of China, the punishment shall be lighter, mitigated, or exempted in accordance with that Law.

Article 52 People's governments at all levels and their relevant departments shall promote the sharing and mutual recognition of regulatory information, implement tiered and categorized supervision based on the credit status of private economic organizations, and enhance regulatory efficiency.
Except for special industries and key areas directly involving public safety and people's life and health where full-coverage key supervision is implemented in accordance with laws and regulations, administrative inspections by relevant departments in the market regulation field shall be conducted by randomly selecting inspection targets and randomly assigning inspection personnel, and the matters subject to random checks and the results of investigation and punishment shall be made public in a timely manner. For multiple inspection matters concerning the same inspection target, they shall, as far as possible, be consolidated or included in the scope of cross-departmental joint inspections.

Article 53 People's governments at all levels and their relevant departments shall establish and improve the mechanism for handling complaints and reports of illegal acts in administrative law enforcement, promptly accept and handle complaints and reports in accordance with law, and protect the lawful rights and interests of private economic organizations and their operators.
The judicial administrative department shall establish a communication mechanism for administrative law enforcement demands involving enterprises, organize and carry out administrative law enforcement inspections, strengthen supervision over administrative law enforcement activities, and promptly correct improper administrative law enforcement acts.

Article 54 The system for punishment for breach of trust and credit restoration shall be improved. In imposing punishment for breach of trust, it shall be carried out in accordance with laws, regulations, and relevant provisions, and proportionate punishment measures shall be taken based on the facts, nature, and severity of the breach of trust.
Where a private economic organization or its operator rectifies the breach of trust, eliminates adverse effects, and meets the conditions for credit restoration, it may file an application for credit restoration. Relevant state organs shall, in accordance with law, promptly lift the punishment measures, remove or terminate the public disclosure of the breach of trust information, and achieve coordinated restoration on the relevant public credit information platform.

Article 55 The multi-channel dispute resolution mechanism shall be established and improved to facilitate private economic organizations in safeguarding their lawful rights and interests.
The judicial administrative department shall organize and coordinate relevant institutions such as lawyers, notarization, judicial expertise, grassroots legal services, people's mediation, commercial mediation, arbitration, and legal consulting experts to participate in resolving disputes involving private economic organizations, and provide targeted legal services for private economic organizations.

Article 56 Relevant industry associations and chambers of commerce shall, in accordance with laws, regulations, and their articles of association, play a coordinating and self-regulatory role, promptly reflect industry demands, and provide services such as information consultation, publicity and training, market expansion, rights protection, and dispute resolution for private economic organizations and their operators.

Article 57 The State shall adhere to high-standard opening up, accelerate the building of a new development pattern with domestic circulation as the mainstay and domestic and international circulations reinforcing each other; shall support and guide private economic organizations in expanding international exchanges and cooperation, and conducting investment and business activities overseas in accordance with laws and regulations; shall strengthen comprehensive overseas services such as legal, financial, and logistics services; shall improve the mechanism for protecting overseas interests; and shall safeguard the overseas lawful rights and interests of private economic organizations and their operators.

Article 58 The personal rights, property rights, and operational autonomy and other lawful rights and interests of private economic organizations and their operators shall be protected by law, and no unit or individual shall infringe upon them.

Article 59 The personality rights such as the right to name, reputation, and honor of private economic organizations, and the reputation, honor, privacy, personal information and other personality rights of operators of private economic organizations shall be protected by law.
No unit or individual shall use the Internet or other communication channels to maliciously infringe upon the personality rights of private economic organizations and their operators by means of insults, defamation, or the like. Internet service providers shall, in accordance with relevant laws and regulations, strengthen the management of online information content, establish and improve complaint and reporting mechanisms, promptly dispose of illegal information that maliciously infringes upon the lawful rights and interests of the parties, and report to the relevant competent authorities.
Private economic organizations and their operators whose personality rights have been maliciously infringed upon shall have the right to apply to the People's Court for measures ordering the actor to cease the relevant acts in accordance with law. Where the personality rights of a private economic organization or its operator have been maliciously infringed upon, causing actual losses to the organization's production, operation, investment, financing and other activities, the infringer shall bear compensation liability in accordance with law.

Article 60 State organs and their staff members, when conducting investigations or requesting assistance in investigations in accordance with law, shall avoid or minimize the impact on normal production and business activities. The imposition of compulsory measures restricting personal freedom shall be carried out strictly in accordance with statutory authority, conditions, and procedures.

Article 61 The expropriation or requisition of property shall be carried out strictly in accordance with statutory authority, conditions, and procedures.
Where property is expropriated or requisitioned in accordance with legal provisions for the needs of public interest, fair and reasonable compensation shall be given.
No unit shall, in violation of laws or regulations, charge fees to private economic organizations, impose fines without a legal or regulatory basis, or apportion property to private economic organizations.

Article 62 The sealing, seizure, or freezing of property involved in a case shall comply with statutory authority, conditions, and procedures, strictly distinguish between illegal gains, other property involved in the case, and lawful property, between property of a private economic organization and personal property of its operator, and between property of the person involved in the case and property of persons not involved in the case, and shall not seal, seize, or freeze property beyond authority, scope, amount, or time limit. Sealed or seized property involved in a case shall be properly kept.

Article 63 In handling a case, a strict distinction shall be made between economic disputes and economic crimes, and the provisions of law on the statute of limitations for prosecution shall be complied with; where production and business activities do not violate the provisions of the Criminal Law, they shall not be treated as crimes; where the facts are unclear, the evidence is insufficient, or criminal liability is not to be investigated in accordance with law, the case shall be dismissed, a decision not to prosecute shall be made, the trial shall be terminated, or a verdict of not guilty shall be rendered in accordance with law.
It is prohibited to illegally interfere in economic disputes by administrative or criminal means.

Article 64 Cross-regional law enforcement shall be regulated, and a system for cross-regional law enforcement assistance shall be established and improved. Where cross-regional law enforcement is required for handling a case, it shall comply with statutory authority, conditions, and procedures. Where disputes over case jurisdiction arise between state organs, they may consult with each other; if consultation fails, the matter shall be submitted to the common superior organ for a decision, unless otherwise provided by law.
It is prohibited to abuse power for purposes such as economic gains to conduct cross-regional law enforcement.

Article 65 Where a private economic organization or its operator has objections as to whether its production and business activities are illegal or to compulsory measures imposed by state organs, it may, in accordance with law, report the situation to or petition the relevant organ, and may apply for administrative reconsideration or initiate litigation in accordance with law.

Article 66 The procuratorial organs shall, in accordance with law, exercise legal supervision over litigation activities involving private economic organizations and their operators, and promptly accept and review relevant petitions and accusations. Where illegal circumstances are discovered, they shall, in accordance with law, raise a protest, issue opinions on correction, or make procuratorial recommendations.

Article 67 State organs, public institutions, and state-owned enterprises shall, in accordance with law or contractual agreement, timely pay accounts to private economic organizations, and shall not refuse or delay payment of accounts to private economic organizations on grounds such as personnel changes, internal payment procedures, or, in the absence of contractual agreement, waiting for approval of completion acceptance or final accounts audit; except as otherwise provided by laws or administrative regulations, they shall not compulsorily require audit results as the basis for settlement.
The audit organs shall, in accordance with law, exercise audit supervision over the payment of accounts by state organs, public institutions, and state-owned enterprises to private economic organizations.

Article 68 Large enterprises, when purchasing goods, projects, services, etc., from small and medium private economic organizations, shall reasonably agree on the payment period and timely pay the accounts, and shall not make the payment of accounts to small and medium private economic organizations conditional on receiving payment from a third party.
The People's Courts shall, in accordance with law, promptly docket, adjudicate, and enforce cases of arrears of accounts to small and medium private economic organizations, and may conduct mediation on the basis of the principles of voluntariness and legality to safeguard the lawful rights and interests of small and medium private economic organizations.

Article 69 Local people's governments at or above the county level shall strengthen the work of guaranteeing account payment, prevent and clear up arrears of accounts to private economic organizations; strengthen budget management, and government procurement projects shall be executed strictly in accordance with the approved budget; strengthen overall guidance on the handling of arrears of accounts, encourage all parties to resolve disputes through consultation, and organize consultation and mediation where major differences exist. In consultation and mediation, the role of organizations such as the Federation of Industry and Commerce and the Lawyers Association shall be brought into play.

Article 70 Local people's governments at all levels and their relevant departments shall fulfill the policy commitments made to private economic organizations in accordance with law and the contracts concluded with private economic organizations, and shall not breach or repudiate the contracts on grounds such as adjustment of administrative divisions, change of government, adjustment of institutions or functions, or replacement of relevant personnel.
Where it is necessary to change policy commitments or contractual agreements due to national interests or public interests, such changes shall be made in accordance with statutory authority and procedures, and compensation shall be given to private economic organizations for the losses suffered as a result.

Article 72 Where expropriation, requisition, or measures such as sealing, seizure, or freezing are implemented in violation of legal provisions, the competent authority shall order rectification; if losses are caused, compensation shall be made in accordance with law; if adverse consequences or effects are caused, the leading personnel with responsibility and the directly responsible personnel shall be given sanctions in accordance with law.
Where cross-regional law enforcement is implemented in violation of legal provisions, the competent authority shall order rectification; if adverse consequences or effects are caused, the leading personnel with responsibility and the directly responsible personnel shall be given sanctions in accordance with law.

Article 73 Where state organs, public institutions, or state-owned enterprises violate laws, administrative regulations, or contractual agreements by refusing or delaying payment of accounts to private economic organizations, or where local people's governments at all levels and their relevant departments fail to fulfill policy commitments made to private economic organizations in accordance with law or contracts concluded in accordance with law, the competent authority shall correct the situation; if losses are caused, compensation shall be made in accordance with law; if adverse consequences or effects are caused, the leading personnel with responsibility and the directly responsible personnel shall be given sanctions in accordance with law.
Where a large enterprise violates laws, administrative regulations, or contractual agreements by refusing or delaying payment of accounts to small and medium private economic organizations, it shall bear legal liability in accordance with law.

Article 74 Where the provisions of this Law are violated, infringing upon the lawful rights and interests of private economic organizations and their operators, if other laws or regulations provide for administrative penalties, those provisions shall apply; if personal injury or property damage is caused, civil liability shall be borne in accordance with law; if a crime is constituted, criminal liability shall be investigated in accordance with law.

Article 75 Where a private economic organization or its operator violates the provisions of laws or regulations in production and business activities, the competent authority shall order rectification and impose administrative penalties in accordance with law; if personal injury or property damage is caused, civil liability shall be borne in accordance with law; if a crime is constituted, criminal liability shall be investigated in accordance with law.

Article 76 Where a private economic organization or its operator obtains commendations, honors, preferential policies, etc., by fraudulent or other improper means, the obtained commendations and honors shall be revoked, the preferential treatment enjoyed shall be cancelled, and punishment shall be imposed in accordance with law; if a crime is constituted, criminal liability shall be investigated in accordance with law.

Article 77 For the purposes of this Law, "private economic organizations" refer to for-profit legal persons, unincorporated organizations, and individual businesses that are established in accordance with law within the territory of the People's Republic of China and are controlled or actually controlled by Chinese citizens, as well as for-profit legal persons and unincorporated organizations that are controlled or actually controlled by the aforementioned organizations.
Where a private economic organization involves foreign investment, the relevant provisions of the laws and regulations on foreign investment shall also apply.
Article 78 This Law shall come into force as of May 20, 2025.
